title: Priority-lane fallback and proactive load smoothing for dedicated pools
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Goal: Implement a priority-lane admission and soft-shedding system for Dedicated pools that enables per-tenant throughput guarantees while preserving tail latency SLOs and minimizing downstream errors. Scope: 1) Priority lanes: requests carry a lane tag (gold/silver/bronzebox/custom) used by the admission layer for weighted token reservation and fast-path routing. 2) Proactive load smoothing: use short-term headroom prediction to preemptively shape bursts into available capacity windows. 3) Soft shedding: probabilistic and score-based request dropping at queue ingress when headroom exhaustion is imminent; accompanied by deterministic fallback rules (route to cheaper model variant / degrade sequence length). 4) Autoscaler integration: expose lane-aware capacity signals and per-lane min-reserve hints to the autoscaler so scaling decisions respect contractual throughput guarantees. 5) Observability: add token-level counters, per-lane queue depth histograms, apology-rate metrics, and end-to-end request traces with admission decisions. Non-goals: rewriting runtime scheduler kernels or customer-visible pricing model changes in this ticket. Design notes: - Admission model: hybrid token-bucket + prioritized queue where tokens are reserved per-lane on admission; tokens represent reserved throughput per window (tokens per-second * slot-size). Tokens can be borrowed across lanes within soft limits for short-lived bursts, tracked with a debt ledger to enable later reconciliation. - Smoothing heuristic: exponentially-weighted headroom estimator using 1s, 5s, 30s windows to detect rising utilization. When headroom < threshold, apply pacing at ingress with probabilistic accept-or-defer decisions and small jitter to avoid synchronization. - Soft-shedder behavior: 3-tier policy: 1) early-bail: cheap early checks (auth, size) to reject obviously invalid requests; 2) score-drop: compute a lightweight priority score (latency sensitivity, customer tier, route importance) and apply probabilistic drop that increases as headroom decreases; 3) graceful-fallback: when dropping would violate SLA, attempt routing to pre-warmed cheaper variant with shorter max-seq or lower precision. - Safety and customer experience: dropped requests return structured 429 with retry-after and fallback hints; golden customers have lower drop ceilings. - Autoscaler signals: emit per-lane pressure (requests/sec above reserved), sustained-borrow-duration, and tail-latency-exceed counts so autoscaler policy can prefer adding nodes before sustained shedding. Trade-offs considered: - We can guarantee throughput by strict partitioning of capacity per-lane, but that leads to lower overall utilization. Hybrid borrowing improves utilization at cost of increased complexity and potential cross-tenant noise. - Soft shedding introduces probabilistic failures which harm UX; mitigations include transparent telemetry and fallbacks. - Adding per-lane autoscaler signals increases coupling between admission and autoscaling subsystems; this is acceptable given Dedicated SLA constraints. Rollout plan: 1) Unit tests + simulation harness for synthetic workloads (1 week). 2) Canary in internal Dedicated cluster with a small subset of tenants and only monitoring enabled (2 weeks). 3) Gradual enablement with conservative thresholds (4 weeks). 4) Full rollout with SLA-backed customers after alpha feedback (by release dedicated-2025.04). Metrics and success criteria: - Apology-rate <= 0.5% for gold over 30 days under target load. - Tail latency (p99) for gold lane no worse than baseline +10% during scale events. - Utilization increase of at least 6% compared to strict partition baseline in mixed workloads. - Autoscaler responsiveness reduces sustained borrowing time by 50% in load tests. Links: design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/PRIORITY-LANE-DESIGN , load tests dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/loads/priority-lane , draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1248
comments: 2025-02-10 - Triage: scoped and prioritized by PM. Suggest splitting autoscaler hooks into a follow-up if timeline slips.

2025-02-14 - Design review with infra and autoscaler teams. Main concern: how to prevent oscillation when tokens are borrowed and autoscaler lags. Action: add sustained-borrow-duration metric and a cool-down before eviction of borrowed capacity.

2025-02-20 - Prototype simulation shows borrow ledger prevents cross-lane starvation in 95% of runs; edge cases at 99th percentile identified where simultaneous bursts occur in gold+silver. Plan: add jittered pacing and backoff windows.
2025-02-25 - Draft implementation submitted (PR 1248). CI flaky on long-running load tests; investigating test harness timeouts.
2025-03-01 - QA: smoke tests pass for routing and token bucket semantics. Blocked on infra change: need metric export for per-lane pressure (ENG-81654) before can enable autoscaler hooks.
2025-03-02 - Added conservative default thresholds and feature flag to gate rollout. Moving to In Progress for implementation and integration testing.
